doc.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Pee Wee Russell as an inimitable individualist
summary: He says only Pee Wee could do Pee Wee and contrasts Armstrong's imitators who stayed individual with today's Clifford Brown clones.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well listen, as long as we’re on a few people I wanted to ask your maybe just reactions to a couple of names I’ll give to you. We already touched on Pee Wee Russell. Touch some more on Pee Wee Russell. What was it about him that was unique? Or maybe he wasn’t.

He was very unique. Any time you want to hear somebody try to sound like him it’s laughable because you know who they’re doing. You know instantly they’re trying to mock — or not really mock but — if you’re trying to do Pee Wee, and I know somebody here who does him very well, but at the same time I can’t take his playing seriously enough because he’s doing Pee Wee. And only Pee Wee could do Pee Wee. You know a lot of guys try to do Louis Armstrong and they ended up really becoming themselves, whether it’s Louis Prima or Harry James or Bunny Berigan or whoever, or Roy Eldridge or Joe Thomas or all the guys that were influenced by Louis, including Rex Stewart too, because he tried to dress like him. Or Vic Dickinson who tried to do a little Louis on his trombone. Well I mean Louis was a great teacher. But I mean he also brought out your own individuality. You could hear twenty trumpet players from that era and all twenty of them sound different. Today you get all twenty trumpet players that try to sound like Clifford Brown and they do. And it’s difficult to know one from the other you see. And so the individuality is gone. Okay. What about Pee Wee Russell? He was such an individualist he was inimitable. You could not copy him without everybody else knowing what you were doing and just making them laugh — ha ha, Pee Wee. This fool is doing Pee Wee. Not to be considered, you know.
